name: Magnetic Field

claims.claim_text: An experimental atomic-level storage scheme that manipulated nuclear spin required a magnetic field of 8.5 tesla, cryogenic temperatures near zero kelvin, and terahertz drive frequencies, and still held state for only a few hundred nanoseconds.
claims.quote_verbatim: They needed an 8.5 Tesla magnetic field. They had to get it down near zero degrees Kelvin.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The Innovation Speculation

claims.claim_text: Transcranial magnetic stimulation can be improvised from an air coil of heavy wire held against the skull: current is built up in the coil and then abruptly interrupted, and the collapsing magnetic field induces current in the motor cortex that produces a visible muscle twitch.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're cutting off the current, right? Right. Assumably with a relay and that then drops the field
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ben Krasnow - Sprauncy Saccadic Spintherism

claims.claim_text: The coupling of a stimulation coil into tissue falls off with the square of distance, so the coil must be held essentially against the skull for the induced field to be effective.
claims.quote_verbatim: Because it obviously drops with the square of the distance.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ben Krasnow - Sprauncy Saccadic Spintherism

claims.claim_text: Field and wave intuition is acquired mainly through years of hands-on experiment rather than study, and many engineers now designing 5 to 20 Gbit/s serial links have no working model of what a magnetic field is or how it affects their circuit.
claims.quote_verbatim: And a lot of them don't have any clue what a magnetic field is or what influence it has on their circuit or how to think about it
claims.speaker: Howard Johnson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Howard Johnson - Winsome Waveform Wizardry

claims.claim_text: Microwave tunable resonators can be built as a small sphere of an exotic magnetic material that behaves like a tiny tuning fork, with its resonant frequency set by an applied magnetic field.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's basically like building a very tiny tuning fork out of a very rare material. It's a sphere of this weird stuff.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An interview with Tony Long - Millimeter Microwave Magician

claims.claim_text: Electromagnetic fields can be made visible by light painting: an LED driven from a detector is moved through the field of a microwave horn while a camera holds a long exposure, tracing out the phase of the wave in space as a sine wave.
claims.quote_verbatim: they actually mapped out a sine wave by moving this horn in space. And then once they captured that on a long exposure shot, it actually shows a sine wave.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Prototyping, Machining & Accelerators- Mugwumps Mulling Milling

claims.claim_text: A magnet implanted in a fingertip gives a tactile sense of magnetic fields: the magnet physically moves in response to surrounding fields, and that movement stimulates the nerves already present in the fingertip.
claims.quote_verbatim: because the magnet is implanted in her fingertip and it moves in relation to fields around it, that then stimulates the nerves in your fingertips
claims.speaker: Jonathan Oxer
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jon Oxer - Innoxious Implant Innovator

claims.claim_text: The stray field from a hard disk drive is strong enough to be sensed at a hand's distance by an implanted fingertip magnet, making disk activity such as a machine going into swap directly perceptible.
claims.quote_verbatim: And the field from the drive was enough to actually be detected in her finger.
claims.speaker: Jonathan Oxer
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jon Oxer - Innoxious Implant Innovator

claims.claim_text: Mains-frequency hum from a transformer is usually mechanical: laminations that are not bonded tightly enough vibrate under the alternating magnetic field and its coupling, and the whole transformer can also vibrate against the chassis.
claims.quote_verbatim: They're not bonded tight enough together and they can vibrate due to the magnetic field and the coupling.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: Finite element analysis, adapted from civil engineering, was used to model the magnetic fields of disk drive actuators so that the force produced per unit coil current could be mapped as a function of angle, since that force response acts as a gain block inside the servo loop.
claims.quote_verbatim: we could model that with the finite elements because we could get an accurate model of the magnetic fields
claims.speaker: Bob Davidson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Davidson - Hoodied HP Hijinks

claims.claim_text: Early hard drives of roughly 100 GB capacity used inductive coils as both write element and read pickup; later generations kept inductive writing but replaced the read pickup with magnetoresistive and then giant-magnetoresistive elements.
claims.quote_verbatim: So the writing is still done inductively with an inductrit.
claims.speaker: Vincent Himpe
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vincent Himpe - Escaped Electron Elocution

claims.claim_text: A GMR read head is externally interchangeable with a Hall effect sensor - current is driven through one axis and a voltage whose polarity follows the applied magnetic field is measured across the other - but the underlying physics is a quantum effect, unlike the Hall effect.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's similar to a Hall effect sensor. You send the current through it one way, you measure voltage across from it. And under the influence of a magnetic field, you will get a positive or a negative polarity out of it. But it has nothing to do with a Hall effect.
claims.speaker: Vincent Himpe
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vincent Himpe - Escaped Electron Elocution

claims.claim_text: A very large transient current can in principle be measured without contact by placing a coil around the conductor and sensing the magnetic field it produces.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you whacked a coil around the tube, you know, could you actually measure the magnetic field from it, right?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Questioning Everyday Prototyping - Verrucose Vehicle Vitilitigation

claims.claim_text: Signal propagation on an interconnect is self-sustaining: applying a voltage between signal and return creates a changing electric field, which generates a changing magnetic field, which in turn regenerates the electric field, so the wave propagates down the line rather than appearing everywhere at once.
claims.quote_verbatim: that changing electric field generates a changing magnetic field that generates a changing electric field, and that self-propagates
claims.speaker: Eric Bogatin
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets

claims.claim_text: Inductance is best defined as the efficiency with which a conductor generates rings of magnetic field lines, specifically the ratio of webers of field lines to amperes of current; doubling the current doubles the field lines but leaves the ratio unchanged.
claims.quote_verbatim: It is the ratio of the number of webers of field lines per amp of current.
claims.speaker: Eric Bogatin
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets

claims.claim_text: Three physical properties set the inductance of an interconnect: width, length, and proximity to the return path. Spreading current over a wider conductor produces fewer rings of field lines, and a shorter conductor has fewer rings to count.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's the width. The more I can spread out the current, the fewer rings of field lines that I get.
claims.speaker: Eric Bogatin
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets

claims.claim_text: Bringing the return path closer to the signal conductor lowers inductance because the return current circulates its field lines in the opposite direction and cancels those of the forward current.
claims.quote_verbatim: The return current is going in the opposite direction. It generates rings of field lines around that first conductor in the opposite direction. It helps to cancel them out.
claims.speaker: Eric Bogatin
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets

claims.claim_text: Placing power and ground planes close together reduces loop inductance because the counter-propagating plane currents cancel each other's field lines, which in turn reduces the voltage developed when the current changes.
claims.quote_verbatim: And we have less total number of rings of field lines, less inductance, and less voltage generated when the current changes.
claims.speaker: Eric Bogatin
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets

claims.claim_text: Non-inductive wirewound resistors rely on the same cancellation principle: the winding is arranged so that adjacent turns carry current in opposing directions and their magnetic field contributions cancel.
claims.quote_verbatim: this is why you can get non-inductive wound resistors, because they're wound a certain way where they cancel out
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets

claims.claim_text: Around a current-carrying wire the electric field extends radially, at right angles to the wire, while the magnetic field forms circles around the wire whose direction follows the right-hand rule.
claims.quote_verbatim: your E field radiates, well, radially, you know, comes off at right angles to the wire. And your M field is circular around the wire.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Call In Show #4

claims.claim_text: High-speed imaging of a high-current power distribution test can show conductors physically flinging apart under the magnetic forces produced by the current they carry.
claims.quote_verbatim: a high current power distribution test where you want to see if your wires are going to fling apart through the magnetic field
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with David Kronstein (Tesla500)

claims.claim_text: Uranium-235 makes up about 0.7 percent of mined uranium, and separating it from U-238 is difficult because the two isotopes are chemically identical.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's 0.7% of the uranium that you mine out of the ground
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer
claims.episode_title: Wait, why is Jeff glowing?

claims.claim_text: Calutrons, a form of cyclotron used at Oak Ridge for isotope separation, work by ionizing uranium and bending the ion beam in a magnetic field; because the two isotopes differ in mass they follow different radii and land in separate collection buckets.
claims.quote_verbatim: It uses magnetic fields and the different weights of those two materials.
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer
claims.episode_title: Wait, why is Jeff glowing?

claims.claim_text: Motor inrush current is large enough that the magnetic fields it produces make industrial bus bars physically rattle against one another.
claims.quote_verbatim: You actually know it when you see like bus bar rattle because the amount of current that's flowing through it from like the inrush current of a motor.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Davis

claims.claim_text: Bus bar temperature is monitored in industrial installations because repeated magnetic rattling loosens joints, loose joints begin micro-arcing, and an arc to ground at tens of thousands of amps is destructive.
claims.quote_verbatim: when things rattle, connections come loose, it starts creating micro-arching situations
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Davis

claims.claim_text: Kirchhoff's current law is a special-case derivation of Maxwell's equations and does not hold in the presence of a changing magnetic field, which is exactly what an inductor produces; in that situation the measured currents and voltages around a loop do not sum as the law predicts.
claims.quote_verbatim: according to Maxwell's equations, Kirchhoff's current law is just a special derivation of Maxwell's equations. Right? It's just – and it doesn't hold in the presence of a magnetic field.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Grow A Superbrain

claims.claim_text: Lumped circuit modelling is valid only while structures are small compared with the wavelength; then energy stored electrostatically can be labelled a capacitor and energy stored in the magnetic field an inductor. When structure size approaches the wavelength the stored energy becomes distributed and those labels no longer separate.
claims.quote_verbatim: If it's stored in the magnetic field, you call that an inductor. And as long as the objects are small compared to wavelength, you can make that, uh, one-to-one identification.
claims.speaker: Tom Lee
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Tom Lee

claims.claim_text: Close to a radiating product, especially where large currents flow, emissions are predominantly magnetic, so near-field EMC probing uses an H-field probe - a small loop that can be built for a few dollars - held directly over the suspect component.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you're up close, that's primarily a – especially for currents, like for large currents, that's a magnetic field. So that's when you use a – what's called a H-field probe.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Keyzermas Vacation

claims.claim_text: The spin of an electron is the fundamental microscopic magnetic dipole of elementary particles; placed in a magnetic field it takes two basis states, up and down, which can encode a quantum bit.
claims.quote_verbatim: The spin is the fundamental microscopic magnetic dipole of elementary particles like electrons, protons, and neutrons.
claims.speaker: Andrea Morello
claims.episode_title: Quantum Computing with Andrea Morello

claims.claim_text: One tesla is a strong laboratory field for reference: the Earth's magnetic field in Sydney is roughly 60 microtesla, while a strong neodymium magnet reaches about 1.3 tesla, which is why small arrays of permanent magnets can substitute for a superconducting magnet in spin qubit work.
claims.quote_verbatim: the Earth magnetic field in Sydney is about 60 microtesla
claims.speaker: Andrea Morello
claims.episode_title: Quantum Computing with Andrea Morello

claims.claim_text: An electron spin in a one tesla field has a spin-up to spin-down energy splitting equivalent to 1.3 kelvin, which sets a hard operating ceiling: above that temperature thermal noise swamps the state distinction, forcing the use of dilution refrigerators.
claims.quote_verbatim: an electron spin in a one Tesla magnetic field has an energy difference between the spin down and the spin up state that is equivalent to 1.3 Kelvin. That is why you can't have anything above 1.3 Kelvin because then the thermal noise would be higher.
claims.speaker: Andrea Morello
claims.episode_title: Quantum Computing with Andrea Morello

claims.claim_text: The nitrogen vacancy centre in diamond carries a spin whose energy splitting is created by the crystal field rather than an applied magnetic field, giving an intrinsic splitting of 2.7 GHz that an external field can then shift.
claims.quote_verbatim: So, you don't even need a magnetic field for it. If you apply magnetic field, you can shift it a bit. But it has an intrinsic splitting of 2.7 GHz
claims.speaker: Andrea Morello
claims.episode_title: Quantum Computing with Andrea Morello

claims.claim_text: In the near field, closer than a wavelength from the source, the magnetic (H) and electric (E) fields exist separately and require different probes; only at a distance on the order of a fraction of a wavelength do they combine into the familiar electromagnetic wave.
claims.quote_verbatim: the magnetic field and the electric field actually start to combine to become your electromagnetic field
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: A Keyzermas Story

claims.claim_text: Anything conductive placed within the near field of a radiator readily becomes part of the antenna and can dramatically alter its radiation pattern, an effect that is much weaker in the far field.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you put something in the near field, it's easy to become a part of the antenna
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: A Keyzermas Story

claims.claim_text: EMC chambers are intended to measure in the far field over a range typically running from 30 MHz to several gigahertz, but at the low-frequency end a small chamber is not physically large enough, so correction factors of contested accuracy are applied instead.
claims.quote_verbatim: At the low end, the chamber might not be big enough. And there's these correction factors that are applied.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: A Keyzermas Story

claims.claim_text: Electromagnetic fault injection drives a powerful current pulse through a small inductor held over a target chip; because the induced field follows V = L di/dt, a large rate of current change is what produces a strong enough magnetic field to disturb the device.
claims.quote_verbatim: So really what you need is a big current change to generate a strong magnetic field.
claims.speaker: Colin O'Flynn
claims.episode_title: Shouting at chips with Colin O'Flynn

claims.claim_text: Whether a voltage exists across a loop of wire linked by a changing magnetic field depends on the definition used: treating voltage as available energy per unit charge means magnetic energy contributes voltage, whereas a strict path-integral definition denies it, so practical engineers and theoretical physicists can reach opposite conclusions about the same measurement.
claims.quote_verbatim: magnetic fields also provide energy to the circuit. And my definition was that voltage is available energy per charge, unit of charge.
claims.speaker: Mehdi Sadaghdar
claims.episode_title: Electroboom!

claims.claim_text: In a demonstration where probe leads are moved around a loop linked by a changing magnetic field, the differing scope readings are real induced effects in the wire and coils; the disagreement is over whether those induced effects are called voltage, not over the measurement itself.
claims.quote_verbatim: But then you know that in his setup, there's been magnetic fields induced in the wire, in the coils. That's what's been showed on the scope.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Electroboom!

claims.claim_text: Circuit theory retains convenient abstractions that are physically inexact, such as conventional current direction and current flowing through a capacitor; in reality charge only accumulates on the plates, but treating the part as an impedance at frequency is easier to work with.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's just a charge build up on the plates and the electrons flow back this way. But in circuit theory, it's more, it's handier to think about, yeah, the current flows through a capacitor.
claims.speaker: Mehdi Sadaghdar
claims.episode_title: Electroboom!

claims.claim_text: A do-it-yourself transcranial magnetic stimulation setup passes a large impulse current through a coil to create a magnetic field aimed at the motor cortex and produce an arm twitch, but the spatial selectivity is very coarse compared with targeted neural interfaces.
claims.quote_verbatim: basically a huge electric impulse through a coil, which created a magnetic field that he targeted at his motor cortex and it made his arm twitch
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: The Same Wavelength

claims.claim_text: Driving an inductive load stores energy in a magnetic field and returns it later, offset in time rather than lost; on the grid this circulating energy is reactive power measured in volt-amperes reactive (VARs), and VARs control voltage while real power determines frequency.
claims.quote_verbatim: The VARs is what, what tends to control the voltage. The, the real power, like I was saying earlier, that is, that determines the frequency.
claims.speaker: Paul Zawada
claims.episode_title: The Smart Grid with Paul Zawada

claims.claim_text: Grid loads are inductive in the overwhelming majority of cases, with capacitive loads confined to unusual industrial processes, so generation must be sized to supply the reactive component as well as the real power.
claims.quote_verbatim: in 99% of the time you're going to, your load is going to be inductive. Typically only it's like weird industrial processes. Do you see like a capacitive load?
claims.speaker: Paul Zawada
claims.episode_title: The Smart Grid with Paul Zawada

claims.claim_text: A PCB routing tool can publish a 3D field solution for an uploaded board so the E and B fields can be inspected interactively, which also serves as a check that the simulated curl of the magnetic field around a current follows the right-hand rule.
claims.quote_verbatim: So for our simulator, we do actually publish like a 3D field for the board you uploaded. So you can zoom in, look around, see the fields, move around, see the E field, B field.
claims.speaker: Sergiy Nesterenko
claims.episode_title: Intelligent Routing with Sergiy Nesterenko

claims.claim_text: A PCB coil actuator can be built against an N52 neodymium magnet, the highest available grade, so that energising the flat coil generates a magnetic field strong enough to lift the coil and move light payloads such as a printed wing, a mirror or a ping pong ball.
claims.quote_verbatim: an N52 magnet, so it's, the highest grade, of magnets, so when the coil, is energised, it basically creates, a small magnetic field, that is, like strong enough, to move the coil, upwards
claims.speaker: Carl Bugeja
claims.episode_title: Motors on PCBs with Carl Bugeja

claims.claim_text: Magnetic field results from professional solvers such as ANSYS, CST, FEMM and openEMS can be brought into Blender and rendered on top of the actual PCB geometry, but the pipeline requires substantial glue code because every solver stores and exports its data differently.
claims.quote_verbatim: because each, each solver has its own way of generating the data, how it stores the data and exports it
claims.speaker: Sam Aldhaher
claims.episode_title: Making The Invisible, Visible with Sam Aldhaher

claims.claim_text: Open source electromagnetic solvers such as openEMS write results in the standard VTK format, which can be imported into Blender through its Python console; KiCad and openEMS also expose Python, so the whole chain from board design to field visualisation can be linked with scripts.
claims.quote_verbatim: And it's, it's a VTK format. And so then you can then import that data into, uh, blender via Python.
claims.speaker: Sam Aldhaher
claims.episode_title: Making The Invisible, Visible with Sam Aldhaher

claims.claim_text: Field solvers written directly in Blender's Python environment, released as the electromagnodes add-on, are limited compared with professional tools but are adequate for quickly trying coil concepts before moving a settled design back to a full solver.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's not the same level as the professional tools, but for sort of, sort of basic simulations
claims.speaker: Sam Aldhaher
claims.episode_title: Making The Invisible, Visible with Sam Aldhaher

claims.claim_text: Interactive rendering of perpendicular electric and magnetic fields over real board geometry is a more effective teaching aid than the traditional chalkboard convention of drawing crosses and dots for field direction, because a change to the model updates the visible result immediately.
claims.quote_verbatim: they go up to the board and they start holding their hands up again and they you know drawing x's and the o's into the board
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Making The Invisible, Visible with Sam Aldhaher

claims.claim_text: In a Hall effect thruster a heated cathode boils off electrons that become trapped in an applied magnetic field, creating a region of high electron density; neutral propellant gas flowing through that region is ionised by collision and the resulting positive ions are then repelled out of the thruster by a nearby positively charged plate.
claims.quote_verbatim: they'll get caught in this magnetic field that you've generated in your Hall effect thruster
claims.speaker: Todd Bailey
claims.episode_title: Electric Propulsion with Todd Bailey

claims.claim_text: Hall effect thruster cathodes are thermionic emitters descended from vacuum tube practice, using barium oxide in many designs and lanthanum hexaboride (LaB6) in others.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's barium oxide in a lot of designs and it's lab six, lanthanum hexaboride in a bunch of other designs, but there's an electron donor, uh, which is the cathode.
claims.speaker: Todd Bailey
claims.episode_title: Electric Propulsion with Todd Bailey

claims.claim_text: Electromagnetic radiation originates in time-varying currents: electrons oscillating back and forth generate a complementary magnetic field, and that changing magnetic field regenerates an electric field, producing a self-sustaining field structure that propagates outward.
claims.quote_verbatim: when electrons bounce back and forth in time, they generate a complimentary magnetic field. And then when the magnetic field bounces back, it regenerates electric field.
claims.speaker: Greg Charvat
claims.episode_title: The Terahertz Frontier with Greg Charvat of Teradar

attribution_notes: ep 252: passages flagged ATTRIB-UNRELIABLE. Claims about transmission-line propagation and the webers-per-amp definition of inductance are attributed to Eric Bogatin because the speaker refers to his own book 'Signal and Power Integrity Simplified' and his own 'essential principles'. The non-inductive wirewound resistor remark is a listener-side interjection addressed to Dave and cannot be pinned to a speaker, so it is null.
ep 498: passages flagged ATTRIB-UNRELIABLE; all claims attributed to Andrea Morello, who is describing his own laboratory's spin qubit work in the first person.
ep 523: passage flagged ATTRIB-UNRELIABLE; near-field and EMC-chamber claims attributed to Dave Jones, who refers to his own video on near field versus far field and addresses Jeff by name.

ep 663: passage flagged ATTRIB-UNRELIABLE and labelled Dave Jones, but the N52 magnet description is the guest answering about his own product while the host offers to link to it; attributed to Carl Bugeja.
